decision: Selected the planar centroid of Utah County parcel 59:068:0006 (PARCELID 590680006; owner of record CORRIGAN FARMS LLC; 40.993893 assessor acres; legal description W 1/2 of N 1/2 of NW 1/4, Sec. 35, T6S, R2W, SLB&M). Eagle Mountain City's 20 October 2026 council packet identifies this parcel number as the land rezoned to the RTI overlay for the Corrigan Farms data-centre project and describes a 40.99-acre property owned by Corrigan Farms LLC, matching the county record. The point locates the entitled property, not a building, site plan or surveyed boundary.

computed.method: Polygon returned by the Utah County parcel service with outSR=4326 (layer stored in Web Mercator, EPSG:3857, reprojected by the server); planar centroid with shapely 2.1.1; geodesic area and distances on WGS84 with pyproj 3.7.1 Geod.
computed.coordinate_reference_system: WGS84 longitude/latitude as returned by the service (outSR=4326).

identity_checks: 20 October 2026 council packet, item 14.A background: 'Corrigan Farms LLC seeks to rezone parcel number 59:068:0006 to add the RTI overlay zone to the property to allow it to potentially develop a data center project with a natural gas power plant.'

Item 14.B staff report: 'the rezone of a 41-acre parcel owned by Corrigan Farms LLC to the RTI Overlay Zone'; the rezone staff report gives 40.99 acres, adjacent to existing RTI on the north, east and south and to Utah County jurisdiction on the west.

The rezone exhibit map in the packet marks the subject property at the south-west corner of the mapped RTI area, south of 1000 North Street, with the QTS-labelled parcels to the north and the Meta campus to the north-east, consistent with the county polygon.

The development agreement's Exhibit A (Property) page in the packet carries no legible legal description, so identity rests on the parcel number and acreage stated by the City and the owner of record.
caveats: No site plan, building footprint or street address exists yet; the City's presentation says there is no development proposal at this time and the remaining approvals (RTI site plan, building permits) are outstanding. The parcel is currently used by QTS as temporary construction trailers ('trailer city') for the neighbouring QTS campus; that temporary use is not part of this project. The centroid is up to about 288 m from the parcel corners.
